prompt: One temperature reading says 500°C in a log of room temperatures.
why: Room temperatures sit around 20°C, so 500°C is wildly far from every other reading. A value far from the rest is an outlier.
trap: A single point, not a tail.

prompt: A single customer ordered 10,000 units when everyone else orders 1 to 5.
tells: 10,000 units when everyone else orders 1 to 5
why: Everyone else orders 1 to 5, so 10,000 sits far outside the pattern. A single value far from the others is an outlier.
trap: One customer, not a long tail.

prompt: One student's age is entered as 210, which is probably a typo.
why: No student is 210, so it's far from every other age and probably a typing error. Outliers are worth checking before using the data.

prompt: A sensor shows a single huge spike, then goes back to normal.
why: One reading jumps far above the rest and the next ones return to normal. A lone extreme point is an outlier.

prompt: Before drawing a trend line, the analyst checks one point that sits far from all the others.
tells: one point that sits far from all the others
why: One point far from the others can pull a trend line toward itself. Checking it first is handling an outlier.
trap: The trend is the goal; the point is an outlier.

prompt: A marathon results list includes one time of 45 minutes, far faster than the world record.
tells: far faster than the world record
why: 45 minutes is far faster than anyone has ever run a marathon, so it can't be real. An impossible value far from the rest is an outlier.
